facts.fact_text: Between 9 a.m. and 11.30 a.m. on 18 October 2007 a demonstration was held on the pavement close to Svoboda Square.
The demonstration on 18 October 2007 was held on the pavement close to the building of the Cabinet of Ministers opposite the Constitutional Court of the Republic of Tatarstan.
At 3.45 p.m. on 18 October 2007 the applicant was forcibly arrested at a bus stop.
After being forcibly arrested, the applicant was taken to the Yapeyeva police department in the Vakhitovskiy District of Kazan.

The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences on account of holding the demonstration in the vicinity of the Constitutional Court of the Republic of Tatarstan.
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Kazan Town Hall stated that heavy road traffic and a car park for government vehicles would put the participants' security in danger, as the reason for refusing to approve the demonstration at the proposed location.

The Supreme Court of the Republic of Tatarstan stressed that an administrative arrest was a measure of restraint which could be applied only in the exceptional circumstances provided for by law and that those circumstances had not been present in the applicant's case.

The Supreme Court of the Republic of Tatarstan found that there were no grounds for finding the applicant guilty of committing the administrative offence of disobeying a lawful order of the police under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Kazan investigative committee at the prosecutor's office of the Republic of Tatarstan refused to institute criminal proceedings against the police officers, concluding that the use of force had been lawful and not excessive.
